sections.content: "I think I can afford around $400,000," says the buyer who's pre-approved for $320,000.
Or worse: "I can definitely go up to $600K," says the buyer who forgot to factor in taxes, insurance, and HOA fees.
Mortgage confusion is the #1 reason deals fall apart—and most agents aren't helping the situation.
The Purchasing Power Problem

Buyers today are overwhelmed. Interest rates are confusing. Down payment requirements vary. Closing costs seem to appear out of nowhere. And online calculators give wildly different numbers depending on what assumptions they make.
The result? Buyers either:

items: **Fall in love with homes they can't afford** (wasted time, broken hearts)
**Get blindsided at closing** (surprise costs erode trust)

sections.content: Why Most Mortgage Calculators Fail

items: They don't include PMI, taxes, or insurance
They ignore HOA fees and special assessments
They don't account for closing costs
They give a "monthly payment" that isn't the actual monthly payment

sections.content: 5 Ways to Help Buyers Understand Real Costs
1. Show Total Monthly Payment, Not Just Principal & Interest
Buyers need to see PITI: Principal, Interest, Taxes, and Insurance. Plus HOA, if applicable.
2. Factor in Closing Costs Upfront
Don't wait until the closing disclosure. Show estimated closing costs from day one so buyers can budget properly.
3. Use Real-Time Interest Rates
That calculator showing 6% when rates are at 7% is giving buyers false hope. Use current data.
4. Create Visual Comparisons
Show multiple scenarios: different down payment amounts, interest rate variations, and price points. Visuals make abstract numbers concrete.
5. Provide Branded, Professional Documents
A napkin calculation says "amateur." A professional document says "expert." Your credibility depends on it.
The Agent's Advantage

Agents who take the time to educate buyers on real purchasing power build instant trust. They write fewer dead-end offers. They close more deals. They get referrals from grateful clients who felt prepared, not surprised.
